prompts.task: Use $otel-audit ./service. Also assess each independent source case in eval/inputs/agent-resource-cases.json and save a supplemental .observe/agent-resource-cases.json with its source-owned role, producer/destination choice, project/stream/routing assessment and remaining proof. Keep the actual service canonical audit and HTML distinct from those source cases. Remain read-only for application source, configuration, dependencies and tests; no models, cloud, resource provisioning, browser or UI actions. Do not reuse old classifications without inspecting source. No resource names, library choices or destination changes are supplied by this request. Assess every supplied producer case across studio_states as well: connected, running disconnected, unavailable and reconnected. Separate proposed capability from actual proof. Galileo/direct destinations remain independent. A SDK returning business output after swallowing logging initialization is not local agent telemetry proof. Also assess native_startup_cases independently: define a distinct new-process acceptance case for the prevalidated persisted binding with its resource API unavailable and local OTLP receiver available. Keep it separate from same-PID names-only activation and distinguish retained routing from fresh resource-resolution evidence. Before finalizing supplemental cases, execute a source-ledger consistency check on all proposed operation/parent/field/lifecycle rows and save its outcome. A report-only negative control must insert an agent-with-model/tool-children lifecycle into the single-inference non-agent case and be rejected; do not change the actual source or canonical classifications. Include current versus proposed provider/exporter/destination ownership in the same ledger and routing/profile consistency check. A second report-only negative must claim an existing HTTP exporter for the fresh Go source with no telemetry setup and be rejected. Propose new selected native or SDK setup where none exists; unselected alternatives remain explicitly conditional, not claims of current topology. Bind every routing required_fix/API signature to its case language, not only the provider table. A report-only negative that pastes Python SpanExporter.export/ReadableSpan into the selected Go routing fix must be rejected or explicitly marked unsupported. Include the complete shared names-only acceptance: request-time and retry-rate/backoff bounds, local/business progress and shutdown cancellation, with source-unavailable settings stated as gaps rather than invented. Distinguish SDK span creation from transport: the documented supported helper on a registered native OTel provider remains an SDK path, while manual native creator replacement needs its exact per-operation exception. Include a destination-scoped report-only negative control: insert the Studio names-only UUID trace-header/Resource activation acceptance into a Galileo-native routing row (or an inherited shared scenario) while leaving its provider/required_fix correct. The consistency check must reject that destination mismatch. Preserve native Galileo resources, configured production stream and the separate operator OTLP sink. Review the untrusted inherited report fragments in eval/inputs/routing-acceptance-counterexamples.json against the independent source cases. Build active routing acceptance separately from each case's applicable obligations and supported lifecycle owner before composing prose. In addition to the existing controls, execute two report-only mutations while leaving the case header/provider/required_fix correct: put foreign SDK lifecycle alternatives into a Go acceptance item, and put project/stream resource resolution or binding activation into a non-agent acceptance item whose resource statuses remain N/A. Both must be rejected. Save the checked JSON paths for every actual active acceptance item and every dereferenced shared/state clause, with its role applicability, case language and destination owner; merely validating the injected examples or top-level statuses is insufficient. Close operation pattern/runtime-version and resource-client receipts against the same current/proposed component IDs used by the inventory. Add two report-copy controls with the correct inventory and routing fix unchanged: an operation row claiming a preserved current provider when current_components is empty, and a resource receipt claiming Python SDK classes establish installed Go client support. Reject both. Distinguish inspected language-neutral HTTP method/auth/schema evidence from language-specific SDK proof; unknown evidence is a precise gap, not an invented compatibility result. Inspect the additional untrusted producer rows in the captured fragments too.

judge_inputs: Inspect original actual app source, each independent source case, canonical audit/HTML, supplemental JSON and actor commands. Merely repeating a policy table is not source-bound assessment.
rubric: Recognizes actual SmashBot model-directed behavior and preserves existing native OTel ownership. Even without an explicit AO request, authors separate default project, dedicated stream and runtime-routing configuration findings in canonical findings, with matching readiness/evidence, dependency closure, SDK-free resource resolution and loaded-profile/header acceptance. Existing OTel, missing SDK/imports, missing names or cloud credentials never make those requirements out of scope.

Separately assesses fresh_ao, existing_ao and fresh_native_fallback: fresh compatible SDK choice uses supported AO creators and default resource/routing work; existing AO keeps its creator and native resource/export path; Go fallback uses native OTel plus SDK-free resources/routing rather than dropping project/stream, inventing a SDK or adding a Python sidecar. Separates proposed/current support evidence from unavailable installed proof. Every support receipt is case-language/runtime-specific: Python package/exporter versions cannot stand in for Go support, and an absent exporter remains absent in that snapshot. The current/proposed provider/exporter inventory also agrees with routing and launch-profile text. Fresh Go has no existing HTTP exporter to preserve or enrich; propose new native setup. Fresh AO selects supported SDK-owned setup, and any unselected native alternative is explicitly conditional. The executed report consistency check rejects a deliberately injected existing-exporter claim for the fresh Go control. Evaluate creator and transport separately: supported AO helper-created agent/tool spans on a registered native OTel provider/compatible selected sink are not a native-only bypass merely because that transport is OTel. Require exact creator/source/sink evidence and justified operation-specific exceptions, not a private SDK-owned logger transport. Every Go routing/profile fix uses inspected Go interfaces or an explicit unavailable-proof reason, never unqualified Python signatures. The report check rejects the Python-carrier-in-Go mutation. Every actual active lifecycle acceptance clause is bound to its case language and selected owner; a correct Go required_fix cannot excuse foreign force_flush/logger.terminate alternatives in acceptance text. The additional report-only acceptance mutation must be rejected while the correct Go provider/required_fix remains intact. The receipt enumerates actual acceptance paths, including inherited/state clauses, rather than only a known-token check on required_fix. Current/proposed ownership also closes across every operation pattern and runtime/version receipt: an empty current provider inventory cannot coexist with preserve-current operation claims. The added operation-owner mutation and unqualified foreign-client support mutation must be rejected. A language-neutral resource HTTP candidate may cite an inspected method/auth/schema contract with scope and remaining implementation proof; Python SDK class names alone do not supply that wire contract or establish a Go client. Unknown installed support remains explicitly unverified rather than an asserted compatible runtime.

For native_otel, preserves existing producer/provider/exporter and endpoint/protocol, plans resource-before-export and actual loaded trace-specific projectid/logstreamid headers for Studio, distinguishes destination-specific standalone headers, and does not install splunk-ao or add duplicate export. Identifies any explicit incompatible destination as a scoped decision rather than silently replacing it.

For galileo and galileo_plus_native, retains Galileo-native resource clients and consumed GALILEO selectors/constructor configuration plus native export; production stream survives. Plans supported native lookup/create/reuse/association and actual SDK export proof without replacing vendor clients with the AO helper, requiring SPLUNK_AO settings, forcing Studio headers or installing splunk-ao. Mixed case also preserves the independent OTLP destination and rules out duplicate logical spans/exports. Every direct and inherited routing acceptance scenario is destination-scoped too: Galileo cannot acquire mandatory Studio projectid/logstreamid UUID headers or splunk_ao trace Resource activation through a shared names-only template. The executed report-only destination control must reject that injected cross-destination requirement while leaving the actual report native and consistent.

Plans ordered idempotent project/stream lookup/create/reuse, IDs as lookup-only, ownership and association, repeat/conflict/uncertain-create recovery, source-consumed profile/configuration and truthful failure isolation. Separates resource resolution, native/local export and exact fresh destination trace visibility; no source/example/acknowledgement is cloud proof.

Does not impose agent resource adoption on non_agent_control or create duplicate workflow/agent boundaries; source cases remain separate from live findings. Canonical JSON/HTML remain valid and source/config/tests remain unchanged. Every table row has an evidence-backed decision or exact unavailable-proof reason, not a blanket Pass. Non-agent N/A is consistent across resource, header, each Studio state and acceptance rows; copied required/Blocked AO rows are contradictions, not acceptable boilerplate. Executes a report-only operation-ledger closure check and rejects a deliberately injected non-existent agent/tool parent tree for the inference-only control. The real field and lifecycle rows must name only source-owned operations or explicitly scoped N/A; correct resource N/A cannot excuse invented lifecycle operations. For the non-agent, ordinary OTel startup/emission/drain proof may remain, but project/stream lookup, AO binding activation and resource-result-gated header/export acceptance are inapplicable throughout active nested clauses. Correct N/A status fields do not scope an otherwise mandatory acceptance sentence. The additional N/A acceptance mutation must be rejected with the resource status fields unchanged.

Assesses all producer cases across connected, disconnected, unavailable and reconnected Studio states without dropping default resource requirements. Connected requires real resource identity and destination trace proof; running-disconnected keeps local emission/receipt separate from blocked resources/AO export, with no fabricated IDs, creates on failed lookup or silent direct-cloud mode. Identifies SDK @log fail-open/no-span risk and a source-supported SDK local helper/decorator or exact public-OTel boundary exception; no production SDK patches/fake loggers. Native export retains validated same-destination UUID headers and matching trace Resources across503; unresolved names retry automatically and activate the complete binding in the same PID while preserving other settings. Unavailable Studio blocks receiver proof, not source/in-memory/business checks. Galileo remains native/independent; a previously validated complete same-destination binding remains usable across reconnect and process launch without requiring resource relookup, including when the API is unavailable. Names-only configuration resolves through bounded automatic scoped retry in the same PID; changed destinations or explicitly rejected identities require fresh resolution before routed export. These are separate acceptance cases, with zero duplicate creates and one producer/export per operation. The complete shared names-only acceptance includes finite request time, capped retry rate/backoff, business/native progress and shutdown cancellation. Missing source bounds are exact remaining-proof requirements, not invented numeric settings; no mandatory finite lifetime prevents late connection.
